properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: cut_structure (used today) reports articulation POINTS — single nodes whose removal splits the network. That answers "what is a single point of failure". It does not answer "how separable are these two subsystems", which is a different and equally architectural question.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::max_flow_min_cut (Edmonds-Karp, exact, unused) returns the minimum-capacity set of EDGES whose removal disconnects a source from a target. Read on a design graph: "which contracts would you have to sever to split A from B, and how many?" Edge weights are already coupling weights, so the capacity has a meaning here rather than being invented.

WHERE IT LANDS: dec:mosa-conformance is OPEN and its own text says reflow2 "already computes most of the criteria" for modular open systems conformance. Severability is one of the ones it does not. req:modularity-computed is the standing requirement that severability be computed rather than asserted.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: min-cut needs a SOURCE and a TARGET, and nothing in the design says which two subsystems a user wants separated — so either the user picks the pair (a new question to ask) or reflow2 runs it over community pairs from leiden (defensible, but O(pairs) and the communities are themselves computed rather than declared). Also, low cut capacity is not automatically good: two subsystems SHOULD be coupled where the design says they should be, and a detector that rewards separation everywhere would push toward a design nobody wants — the same over-selectivity trap is_single_point_of_failure already had to be tuned out of.

═══ ADDED 2026-09-28 — from the three-graph primitives review (Anthony with Claude). Evidence beside the idea; nothing settled. ═══
· ⚠️ IF THIS IS EVER TAKEN, THE ALGORITHM IS NO LONGER IN THE BUILD: reflow2 absorbed eight dynograph-graph names on 2026-08-24 and max_flow_min_cut was among the nine files left behind (Cargo.toml note). Adopting it means absorbing it too.
· StoryFlow retired its own adoption of max-flow / min-cut (proposed there for "keystone scenes") on 2026-08-23 — for fleet reasons (the builders no longer existed), not because the analysis was judged worthless. It is the same algorithm with the same source/target problem this idea's counter-argument names.
· A sharper sibling question for reflow2: DOMINATORS on the golden thread — the node every path from a requirement to its delivery passes through — would answer "single point of failure in intent", which neither articulation points nor a min-cut answers.
· The coupling the cut would sever has an independently confirmed shape: reflow2's contract pair (PROVIDES ∘ CONSUMES⁻¹ through an Interface) matches market_graph's supply relation (PRODUCES ∘ CONSUMES⁻¹ through a SupplyChainNode), built with no shared ancestry — a conduit relation, which is what a flow cut measures.
properties.name: OPEN — should severability be computed as a minimum EDGE CUT, not just as articulation points?
properties.rationale: Chosen from the unused set because it maps onto an OPEN decision rather than onto a hypothetical: dec:mosa-conformance already claims most criteria are computable, and this names one that is not.
